_readme: The video machine's chain: a BRIEF from the teardown machine goes in, cut-ready scenes come out. This is the route AFTER teardown — teardown makes the brief, this turns the brief into output (Damon, 2026-09-02). Stages run in order for one piece. Var syntax matches the teardown machine so the two read alike: '=literal' · '@stageN' a prior stage's output · '!today' · anything else is a workspace-relative path, with 'brands/<brand>/...' filled from the run's brand at run time (rule 7). Stage 5 runs once PER SCENE ('scope': 'scene'); every other writing stage runs once per piece. Machine steps are named here so the chain reads as the whole process. The generation sequence every scene runs — voice, then the two stills, then the one clip, then the checks — is SCENE-GENERATION.md, the method page; the stages below are that sequence in the chain's own shape (2026-09-18 evening).

stages.name: Format read
stages.why: rule the shape, and name what the brief has not decided

stages.name: Production document
stages.why: every fact decided once, before generation costs anything

stages.name: Cast
stages.why: the character sheets and boards a new cast member needs before training

stages.name: Identity plan
stages.why: what must be trained before a frame is worth generating

stages.name: Train identities
stages.why: the plan's TRAINABLE rows, executed by components/identity-training
stages.note: machine work, not a prompt — one training run per subject, recorded as lora.json beside the asset in the brand folder

stages.name: Voice — the one read
stages.why: the whole piece read ONCE, one custom voice per speaking role, chunked per scene paragraph and stitched so the read never restarts — never a call per line
stages.note: machine work. It runs BEFORE anything else generates: the track, its timing sheet and one slice per scene are what every beat downstream is timed against, and what a to-camera clip attaches.

stages.name: Ledgers
stages.why: consolidate the anti-drift tables and check them against each other

stages.name: Scene prompts
stages.why: assemble one eleven-section prompt per scene; sections 1-8 verbatim; section 9 is the first frame, the timeline and the last frame, each in its own door's order

stages.name: Platform + preflight
stages.why: the platform detected and the models shown; the batch refused until every gate is green
stages.note: machine/platform.py then machine/preflight.py check — see formats/RUN-PROTOCOL.md

stages.name: Generate frames
stages.why: TWO stills a scene and no more — the FIRST FRAME generated, the LAST FRAME an edit of it naming only the delta — the whole set in ONE batch, because look and identity drift between batches, never within one
stages.note: machine work, not a prompt. The first frame carries the cast sheet; the edit carries two references, the frame first, and is colour-matched back to it. What happens between the two frames is beats on the clip's timeline — a beat is never generated as a still (SCENE-GENERATION.md).

stages.name: Sound plan
stages.why: the bed, the effects and the room tone — everything heard that is not a spoken line

stages.name: Generate sound
stages.why: the bed (or the song), the effects and the room tone, generated from the plan
stages.note: machine work. A SUNG piece generates the song instead of a bed and carries its own vocal — never both. Effects marked CHECK are held until the clips exist, so nothing is doubled over sound a clip already carries.

stages.name: QC
stages.why: inspect every generated scene against what was specified

stages.name: Re-roll
stages.why: a flagged scene regenerates with its deviations named, up to twice; a label failure composites the real packshot instead of redrawing it
stages.note: machine work, not a prompt. What still fails after two re-rolls ships FLAGGED, never silently.

stages.name: Platform + preflight
stages.why: the platform detected and the models shown; the batch refused until every gate is green
stages.note: machine/platform.py then machine/preflight.py check — see formats/RUN-PROTOCOL.md

stages.name: Motion — one clip a scene
stages.why: the scene's two approved frames become ONE clip: the first frame as start_image, the last as end_image, and — to camera — the scene's own slice of the voice track as audio_references, with the prompt in the maker's four blocks. The step that costs real money, run last and only on frames that cleared QC
stages.note: machine work. Nothing else travels on the clip: the first frame already carries the identity, the wardrobe, the room and the light. Duration is the paragraph's, rounded up; no number is chosen here.

stages.name: Motion QC
stages.why: identity hold, product constancy, anatomy, camera motivation, lip-sync class — every clip before it ships

stages.name: Director pass
stages.why: the creative QC the inspector is forbidden from offering — half-second, scroll stopper, dramatization, motion, format register, delivery landed

stages.name: Handoff
stages.why: the pack the editor receives, and what it guarantees

_variation_readme: THE VARIATION CHAIN (Damon 2026-09-02, from the format-variation playbook — method-05). A variation is NOT a new film: the screenplay, blocking, dialogue, mechanics and edit are FROZEN, and only the rendering swaps. It runs AFTER a production is approved, and one approved production feeds unlimited variations — that is the scale multiplier. Stage v3 is deliberately MECHANICAL (machine/restyle.py, not a model): handing approved prompts to a model to restyle is what produced the slop run — it re-planned the film. Note the axis distinction: a VARIATION changes how the film looks. Changing the avatar, problem or angle changes what the film SAYS, which is a new production through stage0b with different inputs, never a variation.

variation_stages.name: Style gate
variation_stages.why: the person names the target style — one question, no debate
variation_stages.note: machine work is downstream of a human choice; nothing generates until a style is named

variation_stages.name: Style formula
variation_stages.why: one canonical string, used byte-identical everywhere, plus the strip table

variation_stages.name: Convert assets
variation_stages.why: characters, world and product converted FROM the refined sources — never re-described

variation_stages.name: Generate converted assets
variation_stages.why: the conversion instructions executed — one styled design per asset
variation_stages.note: machine work. Each conversion is an image EDIT off the approved source, never a fresh generation from text — that is the failure the playbook names.

variation_stages.name: Restyle the prompts
variation_stages.why: style lock prepended · media swapped · photoreal descriptors stripped — and nothing else
variation_stages.note: MECHANICAL BY DESIGN, not a model. Every approved word survives; the tool prints its own diff so the guarantee is auditable.

variation_stages.name: Generate
variation_stages.why: the restyled set, one batch, exactly as the original run

variation_stages.name: Variation QC
variation_stages.why: style hold is the failure this gate exists for — plus identity, product, geometry, blocking, dialogue

variation_stages.name: Re-roll
variation_stages.why: a style-slipped clip regenerates with the slip named; still failing after two, it ships FLAGGED

variation_stages.name: Assemble
variation_stages.why: the same edit decision list and gates as the original — the edit transfers unchanged
